cases.label: Initial household exploration
cases.assessment: Grounding and validation are explicit. Activity Map, Plainspoken Choosing and Behind The Click still share an activity-led framing; a creative reviewer should challenge overlap before selecting several of these.

cases.label: Fresh alternatives without steering
cases.assessment: Adult ambition, a new online activity and shared-space etiquette add useful directions. Rooms Change Jobs and Less Heroic Home remain close to ordinary-life framing; exact uniqueness is not proof of semantic novelty.

cases.label: Calendar steering with varied territories
cases.assessment: Calendar steering is reflected throughout. Invitation, protected time, retrospective review and curiosity offer different questions, although recognition and activity-led evaluation revisit earlier interests.

cases.label: Excluded RTB and missing research
cases.assessment: All six rationales explicitly preserve the excluded RTB. Protected time and practical-fixture metaphors still need review for unintended product implications; they remain non-approved hypotheses.

cases.label: Business context with qualified evidence
cases.assessment: The shop context replaces household assumptions. The checklist remains one fictional interview, not population evidence. Opening List and Before The Sign Turns have related preparation scenes; selection should favor distinct strategic questions.
